claim: DR47-14 closes the lost-terminal wrong-write hazard only for presses that reach the shield's ordinary arm. A surviving reorder tracker is never dropped by a press on a data-dsh-handle target (ROW D), on the spacing popup's input (ROW P), or anywhere outside the stage — and because the tracker rides the surviving recording's document-capture stream, the next button-down drag anywhere in the document can engage it and commit a move against the element the user pressed minutes ago. The plan asserts the opposite in two places.
evidence: Clause 1's re-seed lives INSIDE beginTravelRecording, which is reached only from the ordinary arm: the isFocusableHandleEvent return and the isResizeHandleEvent arm both return before the beginTravelRecording call, and onPointerSuppress is bound to the stage only, so a panel or toolbar press runs neither drain nor re-seed. The lead independently re-opened the handler and confirmed both returns precede the call. Clause 4 removes only paint; the section-3.4b drain removes only reorderSwallowRef; no ruling drops the tracker itself. The surviving onTravel tests only ownsGesture, and the plan itself rules that for a mouse pointerId never varies, so a resize drag's moves and its pointerup all reach onGestureEnd then stop(), which DR47-2/DR47-13 make the reorder gesture's release. Clause 2 does not refuse it (the button IS down during a real resize drag), clause 3 only changes the origin, and an off-parent release clamps to the nearest end slot, so the drop index differs from the source index and the commit condition is satisfied. Acceptance 52 drives exactly the ROW P / ROW D second-press fixture but asserts only immediately after that press and before any subsequent move, so it is constructed so it cannot observe this path.
impact: This is pre-mortem S7 — the phase's stated worst reachable outcome, a silent structural write on an element the user never dragged — reachable through the most common press classes on the canvas, since a resize handle is present around every selection. It is left un-ruled and un-gated while the plan records it as closed, so approving would ship the safety property S7 exists for on the strength of a claim the source contradicts.
required_correction: Rule the reorder TRACKER's liveness explicitly, not just its paint. (i) Add a DR47-14 clause dropping or invalidating the tracker in the same unconditional first-statements block as the swallow and paint drains, ahead of ROW P and ROW D — this closes the in-stage half at the cost of one statement and no new listener. (ii) Rule the off-stage half, where no shield listener runs at all: either gate engagement on a precondition the surviving tracker cannot satisfy, or state explicitly and with its price why an off-stage press cannot reach a commit. Then correct the two places that assert the hazard is paint-only, and route a gate whose fixture is the missing one: acceptance 52's fixture continued into a button-down drag after the handle or popup press, asserting zero insertion-line nodes at S47-3 and zero POSTs at S47-4.

claim: steps is ruled as an op-blind field, so the fold's behaviour for delete, duplicate, insert-after and insert-child is unspecified, and the most literal reading of the ruling makes a delete with steps 5 a five-deletion write in one journal entry, un-refused and ungated.
evidence: Section 3.6's validation table states the accepted set purely as a number that is an integer, at least 1, and at most MAX_REORDER_STEPS, places it after the op check and beside parseExpectForOp, and nowhere restricts it to the move verbs. Acceptance 51 enumerates malformed SHAPES with no op axis at all. The shipped ladder already records this exact failure class one line above the placement the plan chose: parseExpectForOp is selected BY op and is total by construction precisely because an op-blind guard let insert-child through, and the fold site computeStructuralEdit is verb-generic.
impact: This is the one place the phase expands the wire contract, and the no-new-write-class argument rests on it being a repeat count on ONE existing verb. An op-blind steps silently gives four other verbs a repeat semantics nobody designed or gated — a new write capability shipped by omission, on the write path, with no refusal string and no acceptance leg. It also leaves an executing lane a coin-flip between folding generically and ignoring steps for non-move ops, which are different wire contracts.
required_correction: Rule steps BY OP in section 3.6's table — accepted only for move-up and move-down; for every other wire verb, absent or 1 is accepted and any other value is a 400 in the malformed-input family with its own message — and state that the fold loop is entered only on the move arm. Add the corresponding legs to acceptance 51 (delete with steps 2 gives 400, clean git diff, unchanged journal.remaining; delete with steps absent gives 200 as the control), with the RED-when being: validate steps without the op axis and the delete case answers 200 having applied two deletions in one entry.

claim: Acceptance 15 leg (b) — the phase's only gate on the swallow cell's press-time drain, and half of pre-mortem S6 — states as fact a condition its own fixture does not require, so the leg is green under its own mutation whenever the fixture is built the degenerate way.
evidence: Section 3.4b rules the verdict is written true on the tracker's release path iff the gesture ENGAGED and the drop index at release differed from the source index. Leg (b)'s Path then asserts drop index moved because the fixture drags over the panel and releases there. That does not follow: an outside release clamps to the nearest end slot, and the panel is an aside sibling to the right of the main holding the stage, so the clamp resolves to the LAST slot. If the fixture drags the parent's last child — or any child of a two-child parent — the clamped drop index equals the source index, the cell is never written, and the ruled and mutated arms are identical. The plan applies exactly this clause elsewhere and names it as the discriminator: acceptance 12's fixture requires a drop index differing from its source, and acceptance 46 spells out that a release back on a source slot makes both arms issue nothing. Leg (b) is the row that omits it, and section 0's re-sweep this round covered the between-mutation-and-assertion clause only, so this omission was out of its scope.
impact: The drain is what keeps a drag released outside the stage from eating an unrelated later click — a case that exists only because DR47-2 declines pointer capture. Leg (b) is its sole gate. Shipping the row as written means the phase can ship a set swallow cell with no drain and a green suite. The in-lane recovery is unreliable here: the RED-when obligation forbids reworking a non-firing mutation into one that fires against something else, so a lane may reasonably mark it non-discriminating rather than tighten the fixture, retiring a gate a one-clause correction would have kept.
required_correction: Write the missing clause into acceptance 15 leg (b) as a fixture requirement with its reason, in the shape 12 and 46 already use: the dragged element is not the slot the outside-release clamp resolves to, so the clamped drop index at release differs from the source index, because the verdict is written only on a drop index that MOVED. While correcting the row, also name where its browser half runs: 12 and 15(b) are both ruled driven in a browser and both sit in S47-2, whose Touches line names only the spacing-gesture spec while the reorder spec is created at S47-3, so the two legs currently have no home in the story that owns them.
